## TERM-EXTENSIONALITY

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `low`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: extensionality
- Intended sense: extensionality
- Chosen Pashto: د غړو له مخې برابري
- Rationale: Explicitly expresses equality determined by members. Exact theorem and biconditional follow OpenLogic, not a claim that the native witness proves extensionality.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. provisional descriptive term; unattested exact technical label
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «د غړو له مخې برابري» the clearest conventional rendering of “extensionality” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-MOE-P3-SET` (checked_supports): Afghanistan Ministry of Education, mathematics curriculum department. Grade 7 Mathematics, Pashto, 1398. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://moe.gov.af/sites/default/files/2020-03/G7-Ps-Math.pdf — Native set introduction groups teams and records a team with no participants as an empty set. Attests سټ and a concrete collection-to-object explanation.
  - `AF-MOE-P5-MEMBERSHIP` (checked_context_only): Afghanistan Ministry of Education, mathematics curriculum department. Grade 7 Mathematics, Pashto, 1398. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://moe.gov.af/sites/default/files/2020-03/G7-Ps-Math.pdf — Contrasts membership and nonmembership with team examples and symbols. Native term witness only; OpenLogic formulas remain authority.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.

- Rationale: Labels must not collapse three distinct logical conditions. Mere failure of symmetry or reflexivity is expressed as a negated sentence, not as these technical labels.

## TERM-ORDER-KINDS

- Rationale: Native witness uses order terminology and a strict partial order, with precise/relative/incomplete qualifiers. Adopt defined labels consistently; preorder lacks required antisymmetry, partial order need not be connected.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. regional concept attestation; exact labels provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «مقدماتي / جزوي / خطي / کلي ترتيب» the clearest conventional rendering of “preorder / partial / linear / total order” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P178-ORDER` (checked_context_only): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Exact adjective choices differ from the edition and are recorded as regional alternatives; no Pakistani standard inferred.

- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «ونه / ريښه / نيکۀ / مخکينے / ځايناستے / څانګه» the clearest conventional rendering of “tree / root / ancestor / predecessor / successor / branch” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? - Authorities:
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. ## TERM-FUNCTION

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: function / mapping
- Intended sense: function / mapping
- Chosen Pashto: تابع / نگاشت
- Rationale: تابع is directly witnessed. Use feminine agreement, plural تابعې; نگاشت names the assignment/map without confusing it with its graph. The witness uses a mapping loanword; exact chosen map label is provisional.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. regional technical attestation for تابع; نگاشت provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «تابع / نگاشت» the clearest conventional rendering of “function / mapping” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

## TERM-RANGE

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `low`; confidence: `high`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: range / image
- Intended sense: range / image
- Chosen Pashto: د قيمتونو سټ / انځور
- Rationale: Range consists of all actual outputs; image of C comprises outputs obtained from C. Neither must equal the codomain. انځور here means a set image, not the diagram or graph. Later inspection of the Bukovský/Niazman set-theory text provides the cited concept-specific evidence; chosen descriptive forms remain editorial choices. The native composition order and codomain convention differ, so OpenLogic controls them.
- Confidence reason: supported by the cited evidence; still open to correction. concept strengthened by later native set-theory consultation; retain earlier surface-choice uncertainty
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «د قيمتونو سټ / انځور» the clearest conventional rendering of “range / image” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P110-OPERATION` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Native continuation of definition 1.13 interprets a k-place operation as f:M^k to M and discusses values of variables. Supports operation, value and multiple-input concepts, not the particular OpenLogic conventions about codomains or partial domains. Afghan Pashto regional comparator; rendered page visually inspected for this functions batch.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P23-FUNCTION-DOMAIN` (checked_supports): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Native explanation treats a mapping as a single-valued graph and explicitly defines domain D(f) and range H(f). Its initial relation-based definition allows partial domains; OpenLogic controls totality and specified codomain conventions. Rendered page visually inspected; Afghan regional comparator.

## TERM-FUNCTION-ARGUMENT

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: input / argument / output / value
- Intended sense: input / argument / output / value
- Chosen Pashto: ننوت / ارګومېنټ / وت / قيمت
- Rationale: ننوت and وت are explicitly introduced as supplied input and returned output. ارګومېنټ denotes a function input, not an argument in a proof. قيمت denotes the assigned value, not monetary price.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. regional value concept; other exact labels provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «ننوت / ارګومېنټ / وت / قيمت» the clearest conventional rendering of “input / argument / output / value” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

## TERM-INJECTIVE

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `low`; confidence: `high`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: injective / injection
- Intended sense: injective / injection
- Chosen Pashto: يو پر يو / يو پر يو تابع
- Rationale: At most one input per codomain value; two inputs with equal outputs must coincide. This does not imply every codomain point is attained. Preserve upstream token keys. Later inspection of the Bukovský/Niazman set-theory text provides the cited concept-specific evidence; chosen descriptive forms remain editorial choices. The native composition order and codomain convention differ, so OpenLogic controls them.
- Confidence reason: supported by the cited evidence; still open to correction. concept strengthened by later native set-theory consultation; retain earlier surface-choice uncertainty
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «يو پر يو / يو پر يو تابع» the clearest conventional rendering of “injective / injection” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P147-FUNCTIONS` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Native number-theoretic exposition defines zero, successor and projection functions and builds new functions by substitution and recursion. Supports تابع and the successor example, with general composition concept illustrated by substitution. Exact injection, surjection, bijection and inverse labels remain provisional. Afghan Pashto regional comparator; rendered page visually inspected for this functions batch.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P28-INVERSES-TYPES` (checked_supports): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines identity and inverse maps and inverse uniqueness, then defines injective/simple mappings by distinct outputs on distinct inputs and surjectivity by full target range. Native loanword labels differ from provisional edition descriptions. Supports inverse concept, not an exact left/right inverse label. Rendered page visually inspected; Afghan regional comparator.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P87-CANTOR-BERNSTEIN` (checked_context_only): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — States Cantor–Bernstein: injections/cardinal inequalities in both directions imply equal cardinality, and begins a piecewise bijection proof. Direct native theorem witness. OpenLogic defers its proof, so the edition does not import this witness proof or claim it as translated source content.

## TERM-SURJECTIVE

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `low`; confidence: `high`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: surjective / surjection
- Intended sense: surjective / surjection
- Chosen Pashto: پر هدف سټ بشپړه / پر هدف سټ بشپړه تابع
- Rationale: Every codomain point is attained by at least one input. Qualifier پر هدف سټ prevents confusion with everywhere-defined total functions. Preserve upstream token keys. Later inspection of the Bukovský/Niazman set-theory text provides the cited concept-specific evidence; chosen descriptive forms remain editorial choices. The native composition order and codomain convention differ, so OpenLogic controls them.
- Confidence reason: supported by the cited evidence; still open to correction. concept strengthened by later native set-theory consultation; retain earlier surface-choice uncertainty
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «پر هدف سټ بشپړه / پر هدف سټ بشپړه تابع» the clearest conventional rendering of “surjective / surjection” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P147-FUNCTIONS` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Native number-theoretic exposition defines zero, successor and projection functions and builds new functions by substitution and recursion. Supports تابع and the successor example, with general composition concept illustrated by substitution. Exact injection, surjection, bijection and inverse labels remain provisional. Afghan Pashto regional comparator; rendered page visually inspected for this functions batch.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P28-INVERSES-TYPES` (checked_supports): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines identity and inverse maps and inverse uniqueness, then defines injective/simple mappings by distinct outputs on distinct inputs and surjectivity by full target range. Native loanword labels differ from provisional edition descriptions. Supports inverse concept, not an exact left/right inverse label. Rendered page visually inspected; Afghan regional comparator.

## TERM-BIJECTIVE

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `low`; confidence: `high`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: bijective / bijection / one-to-one correspondence
- Intended sense: bijective / bijection / one-to-one correspondence
- Chosen Pashto: دوه اړخيزه يو پر يو / دوه اړخيزه يو پر يو تابع / يو پر يو مطابقت
- Rationale: Defined explicitly as both injective and surjective; each codomain point has exactly one preimage. Do not abbreviate to يو پر يو alone, which is reserved for injection. Later inspection of the Bukovský/Niazman set-theory text provides the cited concept-specific evidence; chosen descriptive forms remain editorial choices. The native composition order and codomain convention differ, so OpenLogic controls them.
- Confidence reason: supported by the cited evidence; still open to correction. concept strengthened by later native set-theory consultation; retain earlier surface-choice uncertainty
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «دوه اړخيزه يو پر يو / دوه اړخيزه يو پر يو تابع / يو پر يو مطابقت» the clearest conventional rendering of “bijective / bijection / one-to-one correspondence” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P147-FUNCTIONS` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Native number-theoretic exposition defines zero, successor and projection functions and builds new functions by substitution and recursion. Supports تابع and the successor example, with general composition concept illustrated by substitution. Exact injection, surjection, bijection and inverse labels remain provisional. Afghan Pashto regional comparator; rendered page visually inspected for this functions batch.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.

Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P101-PAIRING` (checked_supports): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Gives enumerations of rationals and integers, defines a pairing function on N squared, and supplies exponential and triangular pairing formulas.   - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P77-CARDINAL-EQUIVALENCE` (checked_supports): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Uses a bijection between naturals and even naturals to state equality of set sizes, then proves reflexivity by identity, symmetry by inverse, and transitivity by composition. Direct concept-specific evidence for equinumerosity as an equivalence relation. The witness uses بوج/equal cardinality rather than the edition adjective همشمېره and reverses composition notation, so only its language and proof structure are adopted.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P87-CANTOR-BERNSTEIN` (checked_context_only): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — States Cantor–Bernstein: injections/cardinal inequalities in both directions imply equal cardinality, and begins a piecewise bijection proof. Direct native theorem witness. OpenLogic defers its proof, so the edition does not import this witness proof or claim it as translated source content.

## TERM-FUNCTION-EXTENSIONALITY

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `low`; confidence: `high`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: extensionality for functions
- Intended sense: extensionality for functions
- Chosen Pashto: د قيمتونو له مخې برابري
- Rationale: Same domain and codomain and equal values on every input imply equality of functions; distinguish from set extensionality by members. Later inspection of the Bukovský/Niazman set-theory text provides the cited concept-specific evidence; chosen descriptive forms remain editorial choices. The native composition order and codomain convention differ, so OpenLogic controls them.
- Confidence reason: supported by the cited evidence; still open to correction. concept strengthened by later native set-theory consultation; retain earlier surface-choice uncertainty
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «د قيمتونو له مخې برابري» the clearest conventional rendering of “extensionality for functions” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P110-OPERATION` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Native continuation of definition 1.13 interprets a k-place operation as f:M^k to M and discusses values of variables. Supports operation, value and multiple-input concepts, not the particular OpenLogic conventions about codomains or partial domains. Afghan Pashto regional comparator; rendered page visually inspected for this functions batch.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P25-EXTENSIONALITY` (checked_context_only): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Explains notation f:A to B by D(f)=A and H(f) subset B, then extensional equality of mappings through ordered pairs/domain/values. Native witness omits specified codomain as part of equality; preserve the different OpenLogic convention requiring common domain and codomain. Rendered page visually inspected; Afghan regional comparator.

  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P147-FUNCTIONS` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Native number-theoretic exposition defines zero, successor and projection functions and builds new functions by substitution and recursion. Supports تابع and the successor example, with general composition concept illustrated by substitution. Exact injection, surjection, bijection and inverse labels remain provisional. Afghan Pashto regional comparator; rendered page visually inspected for this functions batch.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P26-COMPOSITION` (checked_context_only): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Explicitly calls mapping composition ترکيب and evaluates first f then g; domain condition requires f(x) in D(g). CRITICAL notation difference: witness writes f circle g for g(f(x)); OpenLogic writes g circle f. Only linguistic/conceptual evidence adopted; never substitute witness formula order. Rendered page visually inspected; Afghan regional comparator.

## TERM-PARTIAL-TOTAL

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: partial / total / defined / undefined / serial
- Intended sense: partial / total / defined / undefined / serial
- Chosen Pashto: جزوي / هرځاے تعريف شوې / تعريف شوے / تعريف نۀ شوے / مسلسل
- Rationale: Partial allows zero or one output per input. Total is defined everywhere on A, not necessarily surjective. Serial is explicitly defined as each x having some related y; avoid treating the ordinary sequence sense as the definition.

## TERM-ENUMERABLE

## TERM-SET-SIZE

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: size / equinumerous
- Intended sense: size / equinumerous
- Chosen Pashto: اندازه / همشمېره
- Rationale: Size compares membership cardinalities, not spatial extent. Equinumerosity is not equality of the sets or the earlier equivalence-relation label. Infinite sizes follow source bijection definitions. Later visual inspection of the Bukovský/Niazman cardinality theorem directly supports equality of finite and infinite set sizes through bijections and all three equivalence-relation laws; it does not attest the exact adjective همشمېره.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. general equal-cardinality concept directly attested; chosen همشمېره adjective provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «اندازه / همشمېره» the clearest conventional rendering of “size / equinumerous” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-MOE-P10-EQUINUMEROSITY` (checked_context_only): Afghanistan Ministry of Education, mathematics curriculum department. Grade 7 Mathematics, Pashto, 1398. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://moe.gov.af/sites/default/files/2020-03/G7-Ps-Math.pdf — Native elementary exposition distinguishes equality of elements from equality of the number of elements and names equivalent sets. Finite examples only; not evidence for infinite cardinal comparison or the exact chosen equinumerosity adjective. Rendered page visually inspected; Afghan regional comparator.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P99-COUNTABILITY` (checked_supports): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines countability by an injection into N, includes finite sets and N itself, defines listability by a surjection from N, and proves the nonempty equivalence. Explicitly chooses a in nonempty A to extend an inverse outside its range. Native technical basis for enumeration and empty-set distinction; source uses N rather than OpenLogic PosInt. Rendered page visually inspected; Afghan regional comparator.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P77-CARDINAL-EQUIVALENCE` (checked_supports): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Uses a bijection between naturals and even naturals to state equality of set sizes, then proves reflexivity by identity, symmetry by inverse, and transitivity by composition. Direct concept-specific evidence for equinumerosity as an equivalence relation. The witness uses بوج/equal cardinality rather than the edition adjective همشمېره and reverses composition notation, so only its language and proof structure are adopted.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P78-CARDINAL-ORDER` (checked_supports): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines cardinal size no greater than by an injection and strict cardinal inequality by injection without equal cardinality, then gives subset and interval examples. Direct concept-specific evidence for cardinal comparison; the edition keeps OpenLogic cardle/cardless notation and Pakistani phrasing.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P133-CANTOR-THEOREM` (checked_context_only): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — States Cantor’s theorem |X|<|P(X)|, gives the singleton injection, and starts the diagonal contradiction with E={x in X: x notin f(x)}. Direct native proof witness. Its controller analogy, notation and composition conventions are not copied into OpenLogic.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P87-CANTOR-BERNSTEIN` (checked_context_only): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — States Cantor–Bernstein: injections/cardinal inequalities in both directions imply equal cardinality, and begins a piecewise bijection proof. Direct native theorem witness. OpenLogic defers its proof, so the edition does not import this witness proof or claim it as translated source content.

## TERM-PAIRING-FUNCTION

- Source term or construction: pairing function
- Intended sense: pairing function
- Chosen Pashto: جوړوونکې تابع

- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. regional concept and closely related label attested

## TERM-PARITY

## TERM-EXPONENT

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: base / exponent / power
- Intended sense: base / exponent / power
- Chosen Pashto: قاعده / توان ښودونکے / طاقت
- Rationale: Distinguish the exponent from the power expression and its base. In 2 to the n, n is the exponent, 2 is the base, and the expression is a power of 2.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. regional mathematical attestation; Pakistani spelling adapted
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «قاعده / توان ښودونکے / طاقت» the clearest conventional rendering of “base / exponent / power” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

## TERM-DIAGONALIZATION

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: diagonal method / diagonalization
- Intended sense: diagonal method / diagonalization
- Chosen Pashto: قطري طريقه / قطرول
- Rationale: Use قطري طريقه for Cantor’s construction from diagonal coordinates. قطرول is a concise edition verbal noun for diagonalization and remains open to review. Every constructed object must differ from row n at coordinate n; do not reduce the argument to merely drawing a diagonal.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. native diagonal-method phrase attested; compact verbal noun provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «قطري طريقه / قطرول» the clearest conventional rendering of “diagonal method / diagonalization” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P111-UNCOUNTABLE-DIAGONAL` (checked_context_only): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Strong native concept-specific prose; its decimal-real proof is not substituted for OpenLogic binary-sequence or power-set proofs.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P112-DIAGONAL-SEQUENCE` (checked_supports): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). ## TERM-CARDINAL-ORDER

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `low`; confidence: `high`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: no larger than / strictly smaller (cardinal comparison)
- Intended sense: no larger than / strictly smaller (cardinal comparison)
- Chosen Pashto: تر ... لوے نۀ / تر ... کوچنے
- Rationale: No-larger-than means that an injection goes from the first set into the second. Strictly smaller adds absence of a bijection. Preserve direction, and distinguish cardinal comparison from subset inclusion or finite numerical comparison.
- Confidence reason: supported by the cited evidence; still open to correction. general cardinal comparison directly attested; Pakistani surface adapted
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «تر ... لوے نۀ / تر ... کوچنے» the clearest conventional rendering of “no larger than / strictly smaller (cardinal comparison)” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

## TERM-DEDEKIND-CUT

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `low`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: Dedekind cut / proper initial segment with no greatest element
- Intended sense: Dedekind cut / proper initial segment with no greatest element
- Chosen Pashto: د ډېډېکېنډ پرېکون / ناتشه خاصه پيلنۍ برخه چې تر ټولو لوے غړے نۀ لري
- Rationale: A cut is a nonempty proper lower initial segment of the rationals with no greatest member. Use the descriptive پرېکون consistently and do not confuse this order-theoretic initial segment with the finite initial segments used as enumeration domains.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. supporting bound/order concepts attested; exact cut label unattested and provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «د ډېډېکېنډ پرېکون / ناتشه خاصه پيلنۍ برخه چې تر ټولو لوے غړے نۀ لري» the clearest conventional rendering of “Dedekind cut / proper initial segment with no greatest element” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

## TERM-CAUCHY-SEQUENCE

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: Cauchy sequence / limit / tends to zero / convergence
- Intended sense: Cauchy sequence / limit / tends to zero / convergence
- Chosen Pashto: د کوشي لړۍ / حد / صفر ته ورنژدې کېږي / تقارب
- Rationale: A Cauchy sequence here is a function from the naturals to the rationals whose sufficiently late values are arbitrarily close to one another. Distinguish this internal Cauchy condition from already having a real-valued limit, since the construction is intended to produce the reals. Use لړۍ for sequence and an explicit approach-to-zero phrase for the null difference.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. sequence, limit and convergence concepts regionally attested; Pakistani surfaces adapted
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «د کوشي لړۍ / حد / صفر ته ورنژدې کېږي / تقارب» the clearest conventional rendering of “Cauchy sequence / limit / tends to zero / convergence” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

## TERM-RECURSIVE

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: recursive definition / mathematical induction
- Intended sense: recursive definition / mathematical induction
- Chosen Pashto: بازګشتي تعريف / رياضي استقرا
- Rationale: Keep recursive definition distinct from proof by induction. Induction has a base case and a successor-preservation step; a recursive definition fixes new values from earlier ones and requires a separate existence-and-uniqueness justification.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. mathematical induction directly attested; recursive-definition label remains provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «بازګشتي تعريف / رياضي استقرا» the clearest conventional rendering of “recursive definition / mathematical induction” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P17-MATHEMATICAL-INDUCTION` (checked_context_only): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — States mathematical induction for a property of every natural number: the property holds at zero and preservation from n to n+1 yields the universal conclusion. It also proves the principle through the set of naturals satisfying the property. Direct regional concept and proof-language evidence; OpenLogic controls its Dedekind-algebra generalization.
  - `AF-BUKOVSKY-P205-NATURAL-CLOSURE` (checked_context_only): Lev Bukovský; Pashto translation by Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Sets and All That About Them / سیټونه او هر څه د هغوی په هکله (1399 / 2020). Afghanistan; Nangarhar University Science Faculty; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Sets-and-all-that-about-them-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Constructs the naturals as a set containing zero, closed under the successor operation x union singleton x, and included in every set with those two properties. It explicitly connects this minimality property with proof by mathematical induction. Direct native concept evidence for successor closure and the least closed set.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.

## TERM-DEDEKIND-INFINITE

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: Dedekind infinite / Dedekind algebra / successor function / closed under a function
- Intended sense: Dedekind infinite / Dedekind algebra / successor function / closed under a function
- Chosen Pashto: د ډېډېکېنډ له مخې نامتناهي / د ډېډېکېنډ الجبر / تالي تابع / د تابعې له مخې بند
- Rationale: Dedekind infinite means that the set injects into a proper subset of itself. A Dedekind algebra adds a distinguished initial element, an injective successor missing that element, and the least-set closure condition. Do not infer ordinary cardinal infinitude without the surrounding Choice assumptions when the direction matters.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. Dedekind finiteness and successor-minimality concepts attested; algebra compound provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «د ډېډېکېنډ له مخې نامتناهي / د ډېډېکېنډ الجبر / تالي تابع / د تابعې له مخې بند» the clearest conventional rendering of “Dedekind infinite / Dedekind algebra / successor function / closed under a function” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

## TERM-PROPOSITION

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: proposition (truth-bearing statement)
- Intended sense: proposition (truth-bearing statement)
- Chosen Pashto: بيان
- Rationale: Use بيان for a truth-bearing propositional statement. Keep it distinct from a proposition theorem environment, which is rendered as a formally asserted result rather than treated as a formula token.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. regional technical attestation; Pakistani spelling adapted
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «بيان» the clearest conventional rendering of “proposition (truth-bearing statement)” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Definition 1.1 uses بیان for a declarative expression admitting a true/false judgment; useful concept-specific comparator for later propositional logic.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P8-TRUTH-TABLE` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Uses 1 and 0 for truth and falsity, names a truth table, defines negation, and begins the definition of conjunction. Direct regional evidence for truth-value, truth-table and connective concepts; the Pakistani edition adapts spelling and uses its own consistent labels.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P18-FORMATION-SEQUENCE` (checked_context_only): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines a finite propositional formation sequence: each entry is atomic, the negation of an earlier entry, or the result of applying a binary connective to earlier entries; a formula is the last entry of such a sequence. Direct regional concept evidence for formation sequences and formula construction; OpenLogic controls the exact grammar and metasyntactic notation.

## TERM-SEMANTICS

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: semantics / semantic consequence
- Intended sense: semantics / semantic consequence
- Chosen Pashto: معنٰی پوهنه / معنايي استلزام
- Rationale: معنٰی پوهنه names semantics generally. In logic, معنايي استلزام means preservation of truth under every valuation satisfying the premises; do not confuse it with a derivability relation.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. Pakistani semantics label and regional logic concepts attested; compound adapted
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «معنٰی پوهنه / معنايي استلزام» the clearest conventional rendering of “semantics / semantic consequence” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `PK-IQRAM-P2-SEMANTICS` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — Attests the semantics label and نحو in native scholarly discussion. The quoted dictionary definitions are not mathematical model-theory evidence.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P24-SEMANTIC-ENTAILMENT` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines semantic validity of an argument by requiring the conclusion to have value 1 in every joint truth-table row where all premises have value 1, and uses the semantic turnstile. Direct regional concept evidence for satisfaction and entailment; the edition uses valuation-based definitions and preserves OpenLogic notation.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P25-TAUTOLOGY` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines a tautology as a formula whose truth-table value is 1 in every row and relates this to semantic consequence from the empty premise set. Direct regional evidence for the tautology concept and its connection with entailment; Pakistani spelling is normalized in the edition.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P33-VALUATION-SATISFIABILITY` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines semantic consequence using every mapping from propositional variables to 0 and 1, then defines feasibility by the existence of such a mapping making every premise and the formula true. It also relates entailment of a formula to infeasibility of its negation. Direct regional concept evidence for valuation semantics and satisfiability; OpenLogic definitions govern the exact scope and the edition uses a clearer satisfiable label.

  - سيمانتيک (viable_alternative): Recorded for expert comparison; the current evidence and rationale favored the chosen rendering or treatment.
  - معناپوهنه بې له اعرابه (viable_alternative): Recorded for expert comparison; the current evidence and rationale favored the chosen rendering or treatment.

## TERM-TRUTH-FUNCTION

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: truth function
- Intended sense: truth function
- Chosen Pashto: د رښتياوالي تابع
- Rationale: A truth function maps truth-value inputs to a truth value. The native page directly supports the two values and truth-table method, while the transparent compound remains a Pakistani editorial choice.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. truth-value and truth-table concepts regionally attested; exact compound provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «د رښتياوالي تابع» the clearest conventional rendering of “truth function” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P7-PROPOSITION` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Definition 1.1 uses بیان for a declarative expression admitting a true/false judgment; useful concept-specific comparator for later propositional logic.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P8-TRUTH-TABLE` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Uses 1 and 0 for truth and falsity, names a truth table, defines negation, and begins the definition of conjunction. Direct regional evidence for truth-value, truth-table and connective concepts; the Pakistani edition adapts spelling and uses its own consistent labels.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P90-PREDICATE` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Native discussion distinguishes an open sentence from a truth-bearing statement and names Predicate, with the Arabic alternatives mentioned within Pashto exposition. Supports predicate-versus-proposition distinctions; not evidence for metaphysical identity.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.

  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P18-FORMATION-SEQUENCE` (checked_context_only): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines a finite propositional formation sequence: each entry is atomic, the negation of an earlier entry, or the result of applying a binary connective to earlier entries; a formula is the last entry of such a sequence. Direct regional concept evidence for formation sequences and formula construction; OpenLogic controls the exact grammar and metasyntactic notation.

Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.

Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. ## TERM-PROP-SEMANTICS

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: truth value / truth table / valuation / evaluation / satisfaction / tautology / semantic entailment / satisfiable / unsatisfiable / contingent
- Intended sense: truth value / truth table / valuation / evaluation / satisfaction / tautology / semantic entailment / satisfiable / unsatisfiable / contingent
- Chosen Pashto: د رښتياوالي قيمت / د رښتياوالي جدول / ارزښت ټاکنه / ارزونه / صدق / تاوتولوژي / معنايي استلزام / د صدق وړ / د صدق نۀ وړ / اتفاقي
- Rationale: A valuation assigns truth values to propositional variables; evaluation extends that assignment to all formulas. Satisfaction is truth under a valuation. Tautologies are true under every valuation, contingent formulas under some but not all, and semantic entailment preserves satisfaction from premises to conclusion. Satisfiability requires at least one common satisfying valuation.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. core concepts regionally attested; Pakistani labels and distinctions editorially fixed
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «د رښتياوالي قيمت / د رښتياوالي جدول / ارزښت ټاکنه / ارزونه / صدق / تاوتولوژي / معنايي استلزام / د صدق وړ / د صدق نۀ وړ / اتفاقي» the clearest conventional rendering of “truth value / truth table / valuation / evaluation / satisfaction / tautology / semantic entailment / satisfiable / unsatisfiable / contingent” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P8-TRUTH-TABLE` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Uses 1 and 0 for truth and falsity, names a truth table, defines negation, and begins the definition of conjunction. Direct regional evidence for truth-value, truth-table and connective concepts; the Pakistani edition adapts spelling and uses its own consistent labels.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P24-SEMANTIC-ENTAILMENT` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines semantic validity of an argument by requiring the conclusion to have value 1 in every joint truth-table row where all premises have value 1, and uses the semantic turnstile. Direct regional concept evidence for satisfaction and entailment; the edition uses valuation-based definitions and preserves OpenLogic notation.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P25-TAUTOLOGY` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines a tautology as a formula whose truth-table value is 1 in every row and relates this to semantic consequence from the empty premise set. Direct regional evidence for the tautology concept and its connection with entailment; Pakistani spelling is normalized in the edition.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P33-VALUATION-SATISFIABILITY` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines semantic consequence using every mapping from propositional variables to 0 and 1, then defines feasibility by the existence of such a mapping making every premise and the formula true. It also relates entailment of a formula to infeasibility of its negation. Direct regional concept evidence for valuation semantics and satisfiability; OpenLogic definitions govern the exact scope and the edition uses a clearer satisfiable label.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P2-SEMANTICS` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — Attests the semantics label and نحو in native scholarly discussion. The quoted dictionary definitions are not mathematical model-theory evidence.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.

## TERM-SUBSTITUTION

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: uniform substitution / simultaneous substitution
- Intended sense: uniform substitution / simultaneous substitution
- Chosen Pashto: يو شان ځايناستي / هممهاله ځايناستي
- Rationale: Uniform substitution replaces every occurrence of one propositional variable by the same formula. Simultaneous substitution applies a listed family at once; do not read it as successive replacement unless a later definition explicitly fixes such an order.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. formula-construction context attested; exact substitution compounds provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «يو شان ځايناستي / هممهاله ځايناستي» the clearest conventional rendering of “uniform substitution / simultaneous substitution” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P18-FORMATION-SEQUENCE` (checked_context_only): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines a finite propositional formation sequence: each entry is atomic, the negation of an earlier entry, or the result of applying a binary connective to earlier entries; a formula is the last entry of such a sequence. Direct regional concept evidence for formation sequences and formula construction; OpenLogic controls the exact grammar and metasyntactic notation.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.

## TERM-AXIOM

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: axiom / axiom schema
- Intended sense: axiom / axiom schema
- Chosen Pashto: بديهي اصل / د بديهي اصل شېما
- Rationale: An axiom is an adopted starting sentence; an axiom schema represents all its substitution instances. Keep individual axioms distinct from the schema that generates them and from premises supplied by a theory.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. axiom and schema concepts regionally attested; Pakistani surface adapted
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «بديهي اصل / د بديهي اصل شېما» the clearest conventional rendering of “axiom / axiom schema” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
- Authorities:
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P37-AXIOMATIC-PROOF` (checked_context_only): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — States a proof of a tautology-preservation result and then lists propositional axiom schemas. Direct regional evidence for proof and axiom vocabulary and for formula-shaped axioms; the edition preserves each OpenLogic calculus rather than importing this particular axiom list.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P39-THEORY-PROOF` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Defines a mathematical theory using a countable sign set, well-formed statements, axioms and a finite set of inference relations; it then defines a proof as a statement sequence whose entries are logical axioms, theory axioms or modus-ponens consequences. Direct regional concept evidence for axiom schemas, inference rules and proof sequences.
  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P48-MODUS-PONENS` (checked_context_only): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Afghanistan; regional comparator only. https://ecampus-afghanistan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Mathematical-Logic-Sultan-Ahmad-Niazman.pdf — Displays modus ponens as an inference rule and proves its admissibility in an arbitrary theory by concatenating two proof sequences and appending the conclusion. Direct regional evidence for the rule name, inference-rule presentation and derivability argument; OpenLogic controls its own derivation formats.
  - `PK-IQRAM-P1-PROSE` (checked_context_only): Bushra Iqram. Pashto Semantics. Pakistan; Pashto Academy, University of Peshawar. https://pashto.org.pk/index.php/path/article/download/46/32/69 — The native prose uses کښې and Pakistani final ے in expository constructions; it distinguishes communication through words and sentences. Consulted for expository phrasing and spelling, not set-theoretic terminology.
  - `GRAMMAR-P166-SOV` (checked_supports): Habibullah Tegey and Barbara Robson. A Reference Grammar of Pashto. Reference grammar; Afghan-central examples, regional comparator. https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED399825.pdf — Word order discussion places modifiers before the verb and treats be-sentence complements as complements, not direct objects. Supports verb-final exposition. Page manually inspected from scan; no OCR text claim.

- Chosen Pashto: فارمول / اشتقاق / بياني منطق / د لومړۍ درجې منطق / بشپړتيا

- Chosen Pashto: د اشتقاق نظام / اشتقاق / قضيه / د اشتقاق وړ / د استنتاج قاعده / ثبوت
- Rationale: Use اشتقاق for the finite formal object and ثبوت for the broader mathematical proof or act of proving. A theorem has a derivation without undischarged external premises; derivability from Gamma depends on the selected system and must not be conflated with semantic entailment.

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: soundness / completeness / consistency / inconsistency / validity
- Intended sense: soundness / completeness / consistency / inconsistency / validity
- Chosen Pashto: سموالے / بشپړتيا / سازګاري / ناسازګاري / اعتبار
- Rationale: Soundness sends derivability to semantic consequence; completeness sends semantic consequence to derivability. Consistency is syntactic and satisfiability semantic, even when soundness and completeness later make the corresponding conditions equivalent.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. validity, contradiction and consistency concepts regionally attested; full property set adapted

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: universal quantifier / existential quantifier / closed term / free variable / bound variable
- Intended sense: universal quantifier / existential quantifier / closed term / free variable / bound variable
- Chosen Pashto: عمومي سور / وجودي سور / تړلې اصطلاح / ازاد متغير / تړلے متغير
- Rationale: A closed term contains no variables. The universal and existential rule schemas retain the source distinction between free occurrences in A(x) and the bound variable introduced by the quantifier; Pashto prose must not weaken those occurrence conditions.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. predicate and open-formula context regionally attested; exact quantifier compounds provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «عمومي سور / وجودي سور / تړلې اصطلاح / ازاد متغير / تړلے متغير» the clearest conventional rendering of “universal quantifier / existential quantifier / closed term / free variable / bound variable” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

- Intended sense: sequent validity / sound derivation system / induction on derivation / lowest inference / semantic preservation
- Chosen Pashto: د سېکوېنټ اعتبار / سم اشتقاقي نظام / پر اشتقاق استقرا / تر ټولو لاندې استنتاج / د معنايي اعتبار ساتنه

- Intended sense: natural deduction / assumption / discharge / introduction rule / elimination rule / premise / conclusion
- Chosen Pashto: فطري استنتاج / فرضيه / فرضيه ايستل / د داخلولو قاعده / د ايستلو قاعده / مقدمه / پايله
- Rationale: Natural deduction is presented as a tree system beginning from assumptions. Introduction and elimination rules add or remove the principal connective, and labeled discharge closes selected assumption occurrences while leaving other assumptions open.

## TERM-TABLEAUX

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: tableau / signed formula / truth sign / branch / root / closed and open branch / cut / eigenvariable condition
- Intended sense: tableau / signed formula / truth sign / branch / root / closed and open branch / cut / eigenvariable condition
- Chosen Pashto: تابلو / نښه لرونکے فارمول / د رښتياوالي نښه / څانګه / ريښه / تړلې او پرانيستې څانګه / پرېکون / د ځانګړي متغير شرط
- Rationale: A tableau is a downward-growing tree of signed formulas. A branch closes only when it contains matching true and false signs for the same formula. Branching rules create alternatives; nonbranching rules extend one path. Cut splits on an arbitrary signed formula, and quantified witness rules retain the exact closed-term and eigenvariable restrictions.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. proof, truth, semantic and predicate roles regionally supported; exact tableau, signed-formula and branch compounds provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «تابلو / نښه لرونکے فارمول / د رښتياوالي نښه / څانګه / ريښه / تړلې او پرانيستې څانګه / پرېکون / د ځانګړي متغير شرط» the clearest conventional rendering of “tableau / signed formula / truth sign / branch / root / closed and open branch / cut / eigenvariable condition” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

- Chosen Pashto: بشپړ سازګار سټ / مشبوع سټ / د هنکين غځونه / د لينډنباوم لمه / ترمي مدل / د صدق لمه / خارج قسمت شوے ترمي مدل

Saturation supplies quantified witnesses; Lindenbaum extension completes the set; the term model uses closed terms as its domain. The Truth Lemma equates satisfaction with membership. When identity is present, the factored term model identifies terms whose equality belongs to the complete set and interprets symbols on the resulting equivalence classes. The compact Pashto construction labels are edition choices; cited Afghan works are regional comparators.

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `low`; confidence: `high`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: structure / interpretation / domain / satisfaction / validity / semantic entailment / satisfiability
- Intended sense: structure / interpretation / domain / satisfaction / validity / semantic entailment / satisfiability
- Chosen Pashto: جوړښت / تفسير / د تعريف ساحه / صدق / اعتبار / معنايي استلزام / د صدق وړتيا
- Rationale: A structure has a nonempty domain and interprets each nonlogical symbol. Satisfaction is first defined relative to a structure and variable assignment. Validity quantifies over all structures, entailment preserves satisfaction from every jointly satisfied premise set, and satisfiability requires one structure satisfying the whole set simultaneously.
- Confidence reason: supported by the cited evidence; still open to correction. semantics, entailment, satisfaction, domain and interpretation roles supported; exact first-order compounds are editorial choices
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «جوړښت / تفسير / د تعريف ساحه / صدق / اعتبار / معنايي استلزام / د صدق وړتيا» the clearest conventional rendering of “structure / interpretation / domain / satisfaction / validity / semantic entailment / satisfiability” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P33-VALUATION-SATISFIABILITY` (checked_supports): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Direct regional concept evidence for valuation semantics and satisfiability; OpenLogic definitions govern the exact scope and the edition uses a clearer satisfiable label.

## TERM-VARIABLE-ASSIGNMENT

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: variable assignment / modified assignment / value of a term / assignment independence
- Intended sense: variable assignment / modified assignment / value of a term / assignment independence
- Chosen Pashto: د متغير ګومارنه / بدله ګومارنه / د ترم قيمت / له ګومارنې خپلواکي
- Rationale: A variable assignment maps every variable into the structure domain. Its x-modification changes only x. Satisfaction of a formula depends only on its free variables, so satisfaction of a sentence is independent of the assignment. Keep this semantic assignment distinct from object-language substitution.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. mapping, value and satisfaction concepts supported; exact variable-assignment compounds are provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «د متغير ګومارنه / بدله ګومارنه / د ترم قيمت / له ګومارنې خپلواکي» the clearest conventional rendering of “variable assignment / modified assignment / value of a term / assignment independence” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

  - `AF-NIAZMAN-P91-PROP-FUNCTION` (checked_context_only): Sultan Ahmad Niazman. Mathematical Logic / د ریاضي منطق. Evidence for تابع in technical Pashto, not a definition of arbitrary set functions. Afghan Pashto regional comparator; rendered page visually inspected for this functions batch.

The preorder example requires reflexivity and transitivity together. Compactness and Löwenheim--Skolem limit which domain-size classes first-order theories can characterize.

## TERM-LOGIC-ORDER-HIERARCHY

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `low`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: many-sorted logic / second-order logic / higher-order logic
- Intended sense: many-sorted logic / second-order logic / higher-order logic
- Chosen Pashto: د ډېرو ډولونو منطق / د دويمې درجې منطق / د لوړې درجې منطق
- Rationale: Sorts separate object domains. Second-order variables range over relations on the first-order domain, while higher-order systems iterate function or relation types. The edition uses one transparent order vocabulary and does not treat these three systems as interchangeable.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. supporting logic, predicate, relation and semantic concepts regionally attested; exact hierarchy labels unattested and provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «د ډېرو ډولونو منطق / د دويمې درجې منطق / د لوړې درجې منطق» the clearest conventional rendering of “many-sorted logic / second-order logic / higher-order logic” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

## TERM-SECOND-ORDER-SEMANTICS

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `low`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: comprehension schema / predicative and impredicative / full and weak second-order semantics / categorical
- Intended sense: comprehension schema / predicative and impredicative / full and weak second-order semantics / categorical
- Chosen Pashto: د ادراک شېما / وړاندوينيز او ناوړاندوينيز / بشپړه او کمزورې د دويمې درجې معنٰی پوهنه / قطعي
- Rationale: Comprehension supplies a relation corresponding to a formula. Predicative comprehension excludes second-order quantifiers from that defining formula; impredicative comprehension allows them. Full semantics quantifies over every relation of the relevant arity, while weak semantics supplies a selected relation domain. Categorical means unique up to isomorphism, not merely detailed.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. supporting axiom, relation and semantics concepts regionally attested; exact second-order compounds unattested and provisional

## TERM-MODEL-THEORY-STRUCTURES

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: reduct / expansion / substructure / theory of a structure / elementary equivalence / automorphism
- Intended sense: reduct / expansion / substructure / theory of a structure / elementary equivalence / automorphism
- Chosen Pashto: راکمونه / غځونه / فرعي جوړښت / د جوړښت تيوري / ابتدايي هم‌ارز / اتومورفيزم
- Rationale: A reduct forgets symbols while retaining the shared interpretations, an expansion adds interpretations, a substructure closes the inherited operations on a smaller domain, and the theory of a structure collects its true sentences. Elementary equivalence concerns the same sentences; isomorphism is stronger, and an automorphism maps a structure onto itself. The edition keeps these roles distinct.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. structure, theory, interpretation, relation and function concepts supported by regional sources; exact model-theoretic compounds and the automorphism label are provisional

## TERM-PARTIAL-ISOMORPHISM

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: partial isomorphism / back-and-forth / quantifier rank / n-equivalence
- Intended sense: partial isomorphism / back-and-forth / quantifier rank / n-equivalence
- Chosen Pashto: جزوي آيزومورفيزم / مخ او شا / د کميت ټاکونکو رتبه / n-هم‌ارز
- Rationale: A partial isomorphism is a finite injective map preserving the relevant constants, predicates and functions on its domain. Back-and-forth extends its domain and range alternately. Quantifier rank counts nested quantifiers, while n-equivalence compares sentences up to that rank. The edition does not collapse these notions into ordinary equivalence.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. partial, relation, quantifier and induction concepts supported by regional sources; exact back-and-forth and quantifier-rank compounds are provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «جزوي آيزومورفيزم / مخ او شا / د کميت ټاکونکو رتبه / n-هم‌ارز» the clearest conventional rendering of “partial isomorphism / back-and-forth / quantifier rank / n-equivalence” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?

## TERM-OVERSPILL

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: overspill / arbitrarily large finite models / infinite model
- Intended sense: overspill / arbitrarily large finite models / infinite model
- Chosen Pashto: له بريده اوښتنه / د هرې کچې متناهي مدلونه / نامتناهي مدل
- Rationale: The overspill argument expands the language by pairwise-distinct constants. If every finite size bound is met, compactness yields a model satisfying all distinctness requirements, hence an infinite model. The descriptive Pashto title signals crossing every finite bound rather than a claim about nonstandard arithmetic.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. finite, infinite, model and compactness concepts supported by regional sources; exact overspill label is a provisional descriptive choice

## TERM-ARITHMETIC-MODELS

- Kind: `terminology`; priority: `high`; confidence: `medium`; provisional: `true`
- Source term or construction: standard model / non-standard model / standard and non-standard element / standard numeral
- Intended sense: standard model / non-standard model / standard and non-standard element / standard numeral
- Chosen Pashto: معياري مدل / نامعياري مدل / معياري او نامعياري عنصر / معياري عددنښه
- Rationale: A standard arithmetic model is isomorphic to the natural-number structure. A nonstandard model has elements outside the values of every standard numeral. The edition keeps model, structure, domain element and numeral distinct and uses معياري and نامعياري consistently.
- Confidence reason: provisional; best available evidence. model, structure, domain, function, relation and countability concepts supported by regional sources; exact arithmetic-model compounds are provisional
- Expert question: In Pakistani Pashto mathematical prose, is «معياري مدل / نامعياري مدل / معياري او نامعياري عنصر / معياري عددنښه» the clearest conventional rendering of “standard model / non-standard model / standard and non-standard element / standard numeral” while preserving the distinctions in the rationale? If not, what exact replacement and inflected forms should be used?
